hook: The fisherman Jesus called "the rock", remembered as the first pope.

pages.x: Simon was a fisherman on the Sea of Galilee, working with his brother Andrew. The Gospels say Jesus walked by and called to them: "Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men." They left their nets and followed him.

Jesus gave Simon a new name, Peter, from the Greek word for rock: "On this rock I will build my church." He also promised him "the keys of the kingdom of heaven", which is why artists paint Peter holding two keys, and why jokes about heaven put him at the gate.

Peter was bold and quick to act. Matthew's Gospel says that when Jesus came walking on the lake at night, Peter stepped out of the boat to meet him, then took fright at the wind and began to sink. Jesus caught his hand: "You of little faith, why did you doubt?"

When Jesus was arrested, Peter followed to the high priest's courtyard. Three times people asked if he was one of Jesus's friends, and three times Peter denied it. Then a rooster crowed, as Jesus had said it would, and Peter went out and wept bitterly.

After Jesus's death, Peter led his followers in Jerusalem. The Book of Acts says that at the feast of Pentecost he preached to the crowds, and 3,000 people were baptised in a single day. He later went to Antioch and, tradition says, to Rome.

Tradition says Peter was killed in Rome under the emperor Nero around AD 64. Feeling unworthy to die in the same way as Jesus, he asked to be crucified upside down. St Peter's Basilica was later built over the place believed to be his grave.
Catholics regard Peter as the first pope, and every pope since as his successor. The church over his grave, St Peter's in Rome, is the heart of the Catholic Church.
pts: One of the twelve apostles of Jesus
